newsitem.title: USA: Kodak sees Danka deal helping earnings.
newsitem.headline: Kodak sees Danka deal helping earnings.

text.p: Eastman Kodak Co said Monday its agreement with Danka Business Systems Plc will help ongoing earnings -- after an initial book loss of about $250 million after-tax.

That agreement calls for Danka to acquire the sales, marketing and equipment service functions of Kodak's Office Imaging business as well as the facilities management business known as Kodak Imaging Services.
Kodak said it would retain and continue to operate the manufacturing and research and development operations supporting Office Imaging.

Kodak characterized the reposition of its Office Imaging business, a process that it would largely achieve through the agreement with Danka, as a move that would have a positive effect on the company's financial performance.

The agreement is subject to certain approvals, including a Danka shareholders' vote, Kodak spokesman Charges S. Smith said. The company expects to close the transaction by year- end, he added, echoing Danka's statement earlier Monday.
Kodak said the transaction would result in a charge of about $250 million in the quarter in which it closes and net cash proceeds of $600 million to Kodak.
"Subsequent to the receipt of the cash, this transaction will be accretive to the company's on-going earnings," said Harry L. Kavetas, Kodak's chief financial officer.
He said the manufacturing operation Kodak will retain is expected to achieve positive earnings from operations by the end of 1997.
After closing, Kodak's remaining Office Imaging business would be focused on research and development, equipment and materials manufacturing, and sales to original equipment manufacturers.
Kavetas said Kodak's Office Imaging revenues will be reduced by about two-thirds, and the net assets supporting that business will be reduced by about 80 percent after the transaction is complete.

"The consolidated Kodak business model, after the repositioning is complete, should have a somewhat higher revenue growth rate on a modestly reduced base, as well as improved operating margins and investment returns," Kavetas said.
He pointed out the company outlined specific objectives when it announced its intention to reposition its Office Imaging business in January of this year.

"At that time, we said that Kodak must reposition the Office Imaging business in order to achieve continued performance improvements, particularly in light of the aggressive targets we have set for all Kodak businesses," Kavetas said. "When complete, this transaction will achieve that objective."
